Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 49, verse 1:

(p-400) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat al-Hujurat (The Chambers).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾

His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿Do not put forward﴾ — concerning it, the scholars of tafsir (exegesis) have three interpretations:

The first of them, which is the most sound and the most apparent, is that it is the imperfect of "qaddama" (to put forward) used intransitively, meaning "taqaddama" (to go forward).

From it comes the phrase "muqaddimat al-jaysh" (the vanguard of the army) and "muqaddimat al-kitab" (the introduction of the book), with the letter dal pronounced with a kasra in both, which is the active participle of "qaddama" meaning "taqaddama".

This interpretation is supported by the reading of Ya'qub, one of the three who complete the ten readers: "la taqaddamu" with a fatha on the ta and a shadda on the dal. Its original form is "la tatqaddamu", and one of the two ta's was elided.

The second interpretation: it is the imperfect of the transitive "qaddama", and the object is omitted to indicate generality, i.e., do not put forward any statement or action before Allah and His Messenger; rather, refrain from that until you act upon the command of Allah and His Messenger.

The third interpretation: it is the imperfect of the transitive "qaddama", but it has been treated as intransitive, and the consideration of its falling upon its object is set aside, because what is intended is the basic act itself, not its falling upon an object.

A parallel to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He is the One who gives life and causes death﴾ [Ghafir: 68], i.e., He is the one characterized by giving life and causing death, and it is not intended in that the two fall upon an object.

And like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?"﴾ [Az-Zumar: 9], because what is intended is that those characterized by knowledge are not equal to those not characterized by it.

Here too, knowledge is not intended to fall upon an object. Likewise, according to this view, ﴿do not put forward﴾ means: do not be among those characterized by putting forward.

We have already established, in our lengthy discussion on the verse ﴿Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?﴾ [An-Nisa: 82], that the expression ﴿before it﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 97] means "in front of it", and we mentioned the verses that indicate this.

(p-401) And the meaning is: do not go ahead in front of Allah and His Messenger, so that you say something without knowledge or permission from Allah. This noble verse explicitly contains a prohibition against putting forward before Allah and His Messenger, and included in this, in the first instance, is the legislating of what Allah has not permitted, the prohibiting of what He has not prohibited, and the permitting of what He has not permitted, for there is no prohibition except what Allah has prohibited, no lawful thing except what Allah has made lawful, and no religion except what Allah has legislated.

We have clarified this extensively with Qur'anic verses in Surat ash-Shura, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whatever you differ over, its ruling is with Allah﴾ [Ash-Shura: 10]; in Surat al-Kahf, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He does not share His decision with anyone﴾ [Al-Kahf: 26]; in Surat Bani Isra'il, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most suitable﴾ [Al-Isra: 9]; and in other places.

His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿and fear Allah﴾ means: by complying with His command and avoiding His prohibition.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾ means: He hears everything you say of putting forward before Him and otherwise, and He knows everything you do of putting forward before Him and otherwise.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 49, verse 2 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, and do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another, lest your deeds become worthless while you do not perceive.﴾

The occasion of revelation of this noble verse is that "when the delegation of Tamim came to the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) advised him to appoint al-Qa'qa' ibn Ma'bad ibn Zurara ibn Adas over them, and Umar advised him to appoint al-Aqra' ibn Habis ibn Iqal over them. Abu Bakr said: 'You only intended to oppose me.' Umar said: 'I did not intend to oppose you.' So their voices were raised, and Allah revealed: ﴿Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet.﴾" Al-Bukhari (a compiler of hadith, known for his Sahih) and others narrated this.

In this noble verse, Allah taught the believers to exalt the Prophet ﷺ, to honour him and to revere him. So He forbade them from raising their voices above his voice, and from speaking loudly to him as some of them speak loudly to others, that is, calling him by his name: "O Muhammad! O Ahmad!" as some of them call out to one another.

They were commanded to address him with an address befitting his station, unlike the address of some of them to others, such as saying: "O Prophet of Allah," or "O Messenger of Allah," and the like.

His saying: ﴿lest your deeds become worthless﴾ means: do not do that, lest your deeds become worthless; or He forbids you from it out of dislike that your deeds should become worthless. ﴿while you do not perceive﴾ means: you do not know of it.

What this noble verse contains of the obligation to revere, exalt and honour the Prophet ﷺ is explained in other passages, such as His saying: ﴿so that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger, and support him and revere him﴾ [al-Fath: 9], according to the view that the pronoun in ﴿and support him and revere him﴾ refers to the Prophet ﷺ.

And His saying: ﴿Do not make the calling of the Messenger among you like the calling of some of you to others﴾ [al-Nur: 63], as has already passed. And His saying: ﴿So those who believed in him, supported him, and helped him﴾ [al-A'raf: 157]. And His saying here: ﴿and do not speak loudly to him﴾ means: do not call him by his name, such as: "O Muhammad!"

Verses of the Book of Allah show that Allah, exalted is He, does not address him in His Book by his name, but addresses him with what indicates exaltation and reverence:

• As in His saying: ﴿O Prophet﴾ [al-Tawba: 73], ﴿O Messenger﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 41], ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 1], ﴿O you who are covered﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 1], although He calls other prophets by their names.

• As in His saying: ﴿And We said: O Adam﴾ [al-Baqara: 35],

• And His saying: ﴿And We called to him: O Abraham﴾ [al-Saffat: 104],

• And His saying: ﴿He said: O Noah, he is not of your family﴾ [Hud: 46], and ﴿It was said: O Noah, descend with peace from Us﴾ [Hud: 48],

• And His saying: ﴿He said: O Moses, I have chosen you above the people﴾ [al-A'raf: 144],

• And His saying: ﴿When Allah said: O Jesus, I will take you and raise you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 55],

• And His saying: ﴿O David, We have made you a vicegerent﴾ [Sad: 29].

As for the Prophet ﷺ, his name is not mentioned in the Qur'an in an address; rather it is mentioned in other contexts:

• As in His saying: ﴿Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him﴾ [Al 'Imran: 144],

• And His saying: ﴿and who believe in what has been sent down to Muhammad﴾ [Muhammad: 2],

• And His saying: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him﴾ [al-Fath: 29].

Allah, exalted is He, has made clear that revering and honouring him ﷺ by lowering the voice in his presence is only from those whose hearts Allah has tested for piety, that is, purified them for it; and that for them, with Allah, is forgiveness and a great reward. This is in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah, those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety. For them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [al-Hujurat: 3].

[p. 403] Some scholars said regarding His saying: ﴿and do not speak loudly to him﴾ that it means: do not raise your voices in his presence as some of you raise your voices in the presence of others.

Al-Qurtubi (may Allah have mercy on him) said in his tafsir of this verse, and his words are: "In this there is evidence that they were not forbidden from speaking loudly absolutely, so that they could only speak to him in a whisper and a low voice. Rather, they were forbidden from a specific kind of loudness, qualified by an attribute: I mean loudness that resembles what they had become accustomed to among themselves, which is being devoid of observing the majesty of prophethood and the greatness of its rank, and the lowering of all other ranks, however high they may be relative to their own." End of the relevant point from him.

The apparent meaning of this noble verse is that a person's deed may become worthless while he does not perceive it. Al-Qurtubi said that he does not have his deed nullified without his awareness, and the apparent meaning of the verse refutes him.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said in his tafsir of this verse, and his words are: "His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿lest your deeds become worthless while you do not perceive﴾ means: We only forbade you from raising your voices in his presence out of fear that he would be angered by that, so that Allah would be angered by his anger, and the deed of the one who angered him would become worthless while he is unaware. As is reported in the Sahih: 'A man may utter a word of the pleasure of Allah, the Exalted, without giving it any thought, and through it Allah writes for him Paradise. And a man may utter a word of the wrath of Allah, the Exalted, without giving it any thought, and it throws him into the Fire further than the distance between the heaven and the earth.'" End of the relevant point from him, in his own words.

It is known that the sanctity of the Prophet ﷺ after his death is like his sanctity during his lifetime. By this you know that the custom prevalent today of people gathering near his grave ﷺ while in noise and clamour, with their voices raised in a disturbing way, is entirely impermissible and unseemly, and their acquiescence in it is reprehensible.

Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) sternly rebuked two men who raised their voices in his mosque ﷺ, and said: "If you were from the people of Madina, I would have beaten you severely."

* *

Two issues

The first: Know that disrespect toward the Prophet ﷺ that implies belittling him, or diminishing him ﷺ, or treating him with contempt, or mocking him, is apostasy from Islam and disbelief in Allah.

Allah, the Exalted, said regarding those who mocked and ridiculed the Prophet ﷺ during the expedition of Tabuk, when his riding animal was lost: ﴿And if you asked them, they would surely say, "We were only conversing and playing." Say: "Is it Allah and His verses and His Messenger you were mocking? Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief."﴾ [al-Tawba: 65-66].

The second issue, and it is among the most important issues: Know that every person must distinguish between the rights of Allah, the Exalted, which are among the specific attributes of His lordship (rububiyya, lordship over creation) and which may not be directed to anyone else, and the rights of His creation, such as the right of the Prophet ﷺ, so that each thing is placed in its proper position, in the light of what the Prophet ﷺ brought in this mighty Qur'an and the authentic Sunna.

Once you know this, know that among the rights specific to Allah, which are among the specific attributes of His lordship, is the seeking of refuge by His servant with Him when calamities overwhelm him, calamities which no one can remove except Allah.

So the seeking of refuge by one in distress, whom calamities surround and misfortunes overwhelm, is permissible only to Allah alone, because it is among the specific attributes of lordship. Directing that right to Allah and sincerely devoting it to Him is itself obedience to Allah and seeking His pleasure, and obedience to His Messenger ﷺ and seeking his pleasure. It is also itself the revering and exalting of the Prophet ﷺ, because the greatest form of revering and exalting him is following him and taking him as a model in sincerely devoting the monotheism (tawhid) and worship to Him alone, exalted is He.

Allah, exalted is He, has made clear in many verses of His Book that the seeking of refuge by His servant in distress, toward Him alone, at times of hardship and anguish, is among the specific attributes of His lordship, exalted is He.

Among the clearest of these are the verses in Surat al-Naml, I mean His saying: ﴿Say: "Praise be to Allah, and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen."﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Say: "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful."﴾ [al-Naml: 59-64].

He, exalted is He, said in these noble, mighty verses: ﴿Say: "Praise be to Allah, and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen. Is Allah better, or what they associate?"﴾ [al-Naml: 59].

Then He made clear the attributes of His lordship that indicate that He alone is the one worthy of worship, saying: ﴿Is He who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you water from the sky, and We caused to grow thereby gardens of delight, while it was not possible for you to cause their trees to grow? Is there a god with Allah? Rather, they are a people who make equals.﴾ [al-Naml: 60].

So these things mentioned, which are the creation of the heavens and the earth, the sending down of water from the sky, and the growing of gardens of delight, whose trees none can cause to grow except Allah, are among the attributes of Allah's lordship. [p. 405] That is why He said after them: ﴿Is there a god with Allah?﴾, meaning one who is able to create the heavens and the earth, send down water from the sky, and cause gardens to grow by it? The answer is no, because there is no god but Allah alone.

Then He said: ﴿Is He who made the earth a stable place, and made rivers within it, and made for it firm mountains, and made between the two seas a barrier? Is there a god with Allah? Rather, most of them do not know.﴾ [al-Naml: 61].

So these things mentioned, which are making the earth a stable place, making rivers flow through it, making firm mountains in it, and making a barrier between the two seas, are also among the attributes of His lordship, exalted is He. That is why He said after mentioning them: ﴿Is there a god with Allah?﴾ The answer is no.

So acknowledging to Allah, exalted is He, that the creation of the heavens and the earth, the sending down of water, the growing of plants and the like, of what is mentioned in the verses, are among the attributes of His lordship, exalted is He, is the truth, and it is part of obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and part of exalting Allah and exalting His Messenger by following him ﷺ in exalting Allah.

Then He said, and this is the point of evidence: ﴿Is He who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him, and removes the evil, and makes you successors on the earth? Is there a god with Allah? Little do you remember.﴾ [al-Naml: 62].

So these things mentioned, which are responding to the distressed when they call, removing evil, and making people successors on the earth, are among the attributes of His lordship, exalted is He. That is why He said after them: ﴿Is there a god with Allah? Little do you remember.﴾

Reflect on His saying: ﴿Is there a god with Allah?﴾ together with His saying: ﴿Is He who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him, and removes the evil﴾. You will know that responding to the distressed when they seek refuge and call upon Him, and removing the evil from those in affliction, is no less among the attributes of lordship than the creation of the heavens and the earth, the sending down of water, the growing of plants, the setting up of mountains, and the flowing of rivers. This is because He, exalted is He, mentioned all of them in one order, in one context, and followed them all with His saying: ﴿Is there a god with Allah?﴾

So whoever directs any of that to other than Allah has incurred the divine rebuke contained in His saying: ﴿Is there a god with Allah?﴾ There is absolutely no difference between those things mentioned in that they are all among the specific attributes of lordship.

Then He said: ﴿Is He who guides you in the darknesses of the land and the sea, and who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy? Is there a god with Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate.﴾ [al-Naml: 63].

[p. 406] So these things mentioned, which are guiding people in the darknesses of land and sea, and sending the winds as glad tidings, meaning bringers of good news, before His mercy, which is the rain, are among the attributes of His lordship, exalted is He.

That is why He said: ﴿Is there a god with Allah?﴾ Then He, exalted is He, declared Himself free of having with Him any god deserving any part of what was mentioned. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Exalted is Allah above what they associate.﴾

Then He said: ﴿Is He who originates creation, then repeats it, and who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Is there a god with Allah? Say: "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful."﴾ [al-Naml: 64].

So these things mentioned, which are the origin of human creation and its return on the Day of Resurrection, and His provision for people from the sky by sending down rain, and from the earth by causing plants to grow, are among the attributes of His lordship, exalted is He. That is why He said after them: ﴿Is there a god with Allah?﴾

Then He, exalted is He, rendered powerless everyone who claims any of all that for other than Allah, saying, commanding His Prophet ﷺ to address them in the form of challenge: ﴿Say: "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful."﴾

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 49, verse 2 (part 2 of 2):

It has become clear from these Qur'anic verses that answering the distressed who call upon Him, and removing evil from those in affliction, are among the distinctive attributes of Lordship (al-rububiyyah), just like the creation of the heavens and the earth, sending down water, causing plants to grow, and placing a barrier between the two seas, and so on through what He mentioned.

That answering the distressed and removing evil from the afflicted are among the distinctive attributes of Lordship, as He, the Exalted, made clear in these verses of Surat al-Naml, is also made clear in other verses, such as His saying, addressing His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And if Allah touches you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him; and if He touches you with good, then He is over all things competent.﴾ [Yunus: 107]

And His saying: ﴿And if Allah touches you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him; and if He touches you with good, then He is over all things competent.﴾ [al-An'am: 17]

And His saying: ﴿Whatever Allah grants to the people of mercy, none can withhold; and whatever He withholds, none can release after Him.﴾ [Fatir: 2]

It is incumbent upon us, O assembly of Muslims, to reflect upon these Qur'anic verses, to believe in what they contain, and to act upon it (p-407) so that we may thereby be obedient to Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ), and exalt Allah and His Messenger. For the greatest form of exalting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is to follow him and emulate him in devoting worship purely to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, alone.

Sincerity in worship to Him, the Mighty and Majestic, alone is what he (ﷺ) used to practise and command, and Allah has said: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, [being] sincere to Him in religion.﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 5] And He said: ﴿Say, "Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion." ... Say, "It is Allah I worship, sincere to Him in my religion. So worship what you will besides Him."﴾ [al-Zumar: 11–15]

Know that the disbelievers at the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) knew with certainty that what was mentioned, of answering the distressed and removing evil from the afflicted, is among the distinctive attributes of Lordship. When calamities overtook them, like the waves surrounding them at sea during storms, they would devote their supplication to Allah alone, knowing that the removal of that is among His distinctive attributes. But when He rescued them from distress, they returned to associating partners with Him.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has clarified this in verses of His Book, such as His saying: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea until, when you are in ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice therein, there comes a stormy wind and the waves come at them from everywhere, and they think they are encompassed, they supplicate Allah, sincere to Him in religion, [saying], "If You should save us from this, we will surely be among the thankful." But when He saves them, at once they commit injustice upon the earth without right.﴾ [Yunus: 22–23]

And His saying: ﴿Say, "Who delivers you from the darknesses of land and sea, when you call upon Him imploringly and privately, [saying], 'If He should save us from this, we will surely be among the thankful.'" Say, "Allah delivers you from it and from every distress; then you [still] associate others with Him."  Say, "He is the Competent to send upon you punishment from above you..."﴾ [al-An'am: 63–65], to the end of the verse.

And His saying: ﴿Say, "Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah comes upon you, or the Hour comes upon you, would you call upon other than Allah, if you should be truthful? Rather, it is Him you would call upon, and He would remove that for which you call upon Him, if He wills, and you would forget what you associate [with Him].﴾ [al-An'am: 40]

And His saying: ﴿And when adversity touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish except Him. But when He delivers you to land, you turn away. And mankind is ever ungrateful. Then do you feel secure that He will not cause the side of the land to swallow you or send upon you a storm of stones, and then you will not find for yourselves a protector? Or do you feel secure that He will not return you into it another time and send upon you a violent wind and drown you for what you disbelieved, and then you will not find for yourselves against Us any pursuer?﴾ [al-Isra': 67–69]

(p-408) And His saying: ﴿So when they board ships, they supplicate Allah, sincere to Him in religion; but when He delivers them to land, at once they associate others [with Him].﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 65]

And His saying: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shadows, they supplicate Allah, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to land, some of them are ambivalent.﴾ [Luqman: 32]

We have previously mentioned, in discussing His saying in Surat Bani Isra'il: ﴿And when adversity touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish except Him﴾ [al-Isra': 67], that the reason for the conversion to Islam of Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl (may Allah be pleased with him) was that when the Prophet (ﷺ) conquered Makkah, he fled from him to the land of Abyssinia. He boarded a ship at sea heading for Abyssinia, and a violent wind came upon them. The people said to one another, "Nothing will avail you except that you call upon Allah alone." Ikrimah said to himself, "By Allah, if nothing else benefits at sea, then nothing else will benefit on land. O Allah, I make a covenant with You: if You deliver me from this, I will go and place my hand in the hand of Muhammad (ﷺ), and I will surely find him kind and merciful." They came out of the sea, and he went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), embraced Islam, and his Islam was good (may Allah be pleased with him). End of quotation.

We have also previously mentioned there that some of those who bear the name of Islam are in a worse state than these disbelievers mentioned, because in times of hardship they turn to other than Allah, seeking from Him what the believers seek from Allah. From what has been mentioned, you know that what has spread in the regions of the world of seeking refuge, in times of distress and hardship, in other than Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, such as their doing so near the grave of the Prophet (ﷺ) and at the graves of those whom they believe to be righteous, claiming that this is part of the religion of Allah and love of the Messenger (ﷺ), his exaltation, and love of the righteous, is all among the greatest falsehood, and is a violation of the sanctities of Allah and the sanctities of His Messenger.

For directing rights that are specific to the Creator, which are among the distinctive attributes of His Lordship, toward the Prophet (ﷺ) or others believed to be righteous, necessitates the wrath of Allah, the wrath of the Prophet (ﷺ), and the wrath of everyone who truly follows him.

It is well known that he (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him) did not command this, nor did any of his companions, and it is prohibited in the law of every prophet among the prophets. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿It is not for a human that Allah should give him the Scripture, judgement and prophethood and then he would say to the people, "Be servants to me rather than Allah," but [instead, he would say], "Be people of the Lord, by what you have been teaching of the Scripture and by what you have been studying."﴾ ﴿Nor would he order you to take the angels and prophets as lords. Would he order you to disbelieve after you have submitted [to Allah]?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 79–80]

(p-409) Rather, what he (ﷺ) used to command is what Allah commanded him to command, in His saying: ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we will not worship except Allah and not associate anything with Him and not take one another as lords instead of Allah." But if they turn away, then say, "Bear witness that we are Muslims."﴾ [Al 'Imran: 64]

Know that every person of sound mind, when he sees a man who claims to be religious, claiming love of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his exaltation, while he exalts the Prophet (ﷺ) and praises him by saying that he is the one who created the heavens and the earth, sent down water from the sky and caused gardens of delight to grow by it, and that he (ﷺ) is the one who made the earth a resting place and placed rivers through it, placed firm mountains upon it, and placed a barrier between the two seas, and so on through what the preceding verses contain, that sane person will have no doubt that this praiser who exalts [the Prophet] in his own claim is among the enemies of Allah and His Messenger, transgressors of the limits of Allah.

You have known from the clear verses that there is no difference between this and answering the distressed and removing evil from the afflicted.

It is incumbent upon us, O assembly of Muslims, to awaken from the sleep of ignorance, to exalt our Lord by carrying out His command and avoiding His prohibitions, to devote worship sincerely to Him, and to exalt our Prophet (ﷺ) by following him and emulating him in exalting Allah, being sincere to Him, and emulating him in everything he brought.

And that we should not oppose him (ﷺ) or disobey him, and that we should not do anything that indicates a lack of exaltation and respect, such as raising voices near his grave (ﷺ). Our intention is sincere advice and compassion for our Muslim brothers, so that they may act by the Book of Allah, exalt His Prophet (ﷺ) in the manner of one who conforms to what he (ﷺ) brought, and abandon what the ignorant call love and exaltation, while in reality it is contempt, disparagement, and a violation of the sanctities of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ). ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it and will not find for himself besides Allah any ally or helper.﴾ ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer – those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, even as much as the speck on a date seed.﴾ [al-Nisa': 123–124]

Know also, may Allah have mercy upon you, that there is no difference between what we have mentioned of answering the distressed and removing evil from the afflicted, and attaining desired things that no one can bring about except Allah, such as obtaining children, wealth, and all kinds of good.

(p-410) For the servant's turning to his Lord in such matters is also among the distinctive attributes of His Lordship, the Mighty and Majestic, as He said: ﴿Say, "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?"﴾ [Yunus: 31] And He said: ﴿So seek provision from Allah, and worship Him and be grateful to Him.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 17] And He said: ﴿He bestows females upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills.﴾ [al-Shura: 49] And He said: ﴿And Allah has made for you from your spouses children and grandchildren and provided for you from the good things.﴾ [al-Nahl: 72] And He said: ﴿And ask Allah of His bounty.﴾ [al-Nisa': 32], along with other verses.

In a hadith: "When you ask, ask Allah."

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, praised His Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions for their turning to Him at the time of distress on the Day of Badr, in His saying: ﴿When you were seeking help from your Lord, and He answered you.﴾ [al-Anfal: 9] Our Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions, when a matter or distress befell them, would turn to Allah and devote their supplication sincerely to Him. So it is incumbent upon us to follow and not to innovate (bid'ah).

Note (tanbih)

Know that it is obligatory upon every Muslim to reflect on the meaning of worship ('ibadah), which encompasses all that Allah commanded to be drawn near to Him through, of all acts of drawing near, so that he makes his drawing near through them sincerely to Allah, and does not direct any part of it to other than Allah, whatever it may be.

And it is evident that this includes the forms of worship. It is therefore not appropriate for one greeting him (ﷺ) to place his right hand upon his left as in the posture of one praying, because the posture of prayer falls within the category of worship, and so it should be sincerely for Allah, just as he (ﷺ) and his companions used to devote acts of worship and their forms purely to Allah alone.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 49, verse 6:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, if there comes to you a defiant one with information, verify, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful.﴾

This noble verse was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'it, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had sent to the Banu al-Mustaliq to collect the charity (sadaqat) of their wealth. When they heard of him, they came out to meet him joyfully, but he feared them and thought they intended to kill him. So he returned to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) and claimed to him that they had withheld the charity and intended to kill him. Then a delegation from them came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him of al-Walid's lie, so Allah revealed this verse. It indicates that the testimony of a defiant person about his report is not to be accepted.

(p-411) Allah, may He be exalted, stated explicitly in another place the prohibition of accepting the testimony of a defiant person, in His saying: ﴿And do not accept their testimony ever, and those are the defiant ones﴾ [al-Nur: 4]. There is no disagreement among the scholars on rejecting the testimony of a defiant person and not accepting his report.

This verse of Surah al-Hujurat indicates two matters:

The first of them: that if a defiant person comes with a report whose truth can be known, and whether what the defiant person said about it is true or false, then verification (tabayyun) is obligatory regarding it.

The second: what the scholars of usul (legal theory) derived from it as evidence for accepting the report of a trustworthy (adl) person. This is because the saying of Allah, may He be exalted, ﴿If there comes to you a defiant one with information, verify﴾ is a condition by the evidence of its implicit meaning (dalil al-khitab), namely the concept of its opposite: that the one who comes with information, if he is not defiant but rather trustworthy (adl), then verification of his report is not required, according to the reading "fa-tabayyanu" (verify), nor scrutiny (tathabbut) according to the reading "fa-tathabbatu," and this is so.

As for the testimony of a defiant person, it is rejected, as indicated by the verse of al-Nur mentioned just above.

We have previously explained the meaning of defiance (fisq) and its types in several places in this blessed book.

His saying: ﴿lest you harm a people﴾ means: so that you do not harm a people, or out of dislike that you harm a people out of ignorance, i.e., because of your assumption that the report brought by the defiant one is true, and so you become, over what you did of striking the aforementioned people, regretful, because the defiant one's lie concerning them became evident. For if they had not verified the report of al-Walid about the Banu al-Mustaliq, they would have treated them as apostates; and had they done so, they would have regretted it.

This letter was read by the majority of the Seven Readers except Hamzah and al-Kisa'i: "fa-tabayyanu," with a single ya' (ب) followed by a doubled ya' (ي) with shadda, then a nun (ن). Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it: "fa-tathabbatu," with a tha' (ث) followed by a ba' (ب) with a doubled ba' and shadda, then a ta' (ت).

The first is from tabayyun (clarification), and the second from tathabbut (scrutiny).

The meaning of both readings is one: the command to be deliberate and not hasty until the truth becomes evident regarding what the defiant one reported.

(p-412) His statement, exalted is He: ﴿But Allah has endeared to you the faith and made it beautiful in your hearts, and He has made disbelief, defiance and disobedience hateful to you.﴾

What He, exalted and majestic is He, mentioned in this noble verse, that it is He who made faith beloved to them and beautified it in their hearts, and made disbelief, defiance and disobedience hateful to them, has come clarified in many verses, in which it is explicitly stated that He, may He be exalted, guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills, such as His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever Allah guides is the one rightly guided, but whoever He leaves astray - never will you find for them a protecting friend to guide them.﴾ [al-Kahf: 17]

And His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever Allah guides is the one rightly guided, but whoever He leaves astray - never will you find for them allies other than Him.﴾ [al-Isra': 97]

And His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever Allah guides is the one rightly guided, but whoever He leaves astray - it is those who are the losers.﴾ [al-A'raf: 178]

And His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And by the soul and He who proportioned it. And inspired it [with the knowledge] of its wickedness and its righteousness.﴾ [al-Shams: 7-8]. Verses of this kind are many and well known. We ask Allah, the Merciful, the Generous, to guide us and not to let us go astray.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 49, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the believers are but brothers﴾.

This brotherhood which Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, affirmed in this noble verse for the believers, one toward another, is the brotherhood of religion (ukhuwwat al-din), not of lineage (al-nasab).

Allah, may He be exalted, has also made clear that brotherhood exists in religion in His saying: ﴿And if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion﴾ [al-Ahzab: 5].

We have already discussed, in the surah of Bani Isra'il, in the commentary on His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most suitable﴾ [al-Isra': 9], that religious brotherhood is greater and stronger than brotherhood of lineage (ukhuwwa nasabiyya), and we explained the evidences for that from the Book and the Sunnah. That suffices, so there is no need to repeat it here.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 49, verse 11:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them, nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them.﴾ His saying: ﴿Let not a people ridicule [another] people﴾ means: let them not belittle them or mock them. The Arabs say sakhira minhu (with a kasra on the kha'), yaskharu (with a fatha on the kha', according to the analogical pattern), when one mocks him and belittles him.

In this noble verse, Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, has forbidden mocking people, clarifying that the one who is mocked may be better than the one who mocks.

Among the worst of ugly deeds is the lowly and base person belittling the most noble and most excellent, and mocking him.

What this noble verse includes of the prohibition of mockery, the censure of its doer and his punishment with Allah, has come in other places, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those who criticize the volunteers among the believers concerning [their] charities and [criticize] those who find nothing to give except their effort, so they ridicule them – Allah will ridicule them, and they will have a painful punishment.﴾ [At-Tawbah: 79].

Allah, may He be exalted, has also made clear that the arrogant disbelievers in this world used to ridicule the weak believers in the abode of this world, and that those [believers] will ridicule the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿The life of this world has been made attractive to those who disbelieve, and they ridicule those who believe; but those who fear Allah will be above them on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 212]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they would exchange winks.﴾ up to His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, upon couches, looking on. Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin: 29–36].

Therefore, it is not fitting for anyone who sees a Muslim in a shabby condition, showing the marks of poverty and weakness, to ridicule him, because of these verses that we have mentioned.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not defame one another.﴾

That is: let none of you defame his brother, as its explanation has already preceded in the surah of Banu Isra'il, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most suitable﴾ [Al-Isra': 9].

Allah, may He be exalted, has threatened those who defame people in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Woe to every slanderer and defamer﴾ [Al-Humazah: 1]. The humazah is one who often gestures at people (with contempt), and the lumazah is one who often defames.

Some scholars said: the hamz is by action, like winking with the eye, out of contempt and disdain, and the lamz is by the tongue, and backbiting (ghibah) is included in it.

Allah, may He be exalted, has explicitly prohibited this in His saying: ﴿And do not backbite one another.﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 12], and He has made people repulsed by it to the utmost degree in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would detest it.﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 12]. Therefore, it is obligatory upon the Muslim to keep as far away as possible from falling into the honour of his brother.

[p. 414]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female﴾.

In this noble verse, He (exalted and majestic) mentions that He created mankind from a male and a female. Here He does not explain how He created the male and the female mentioned, but He explains this in other places in the Book of Allah. He explains that He created that male, who is Adam, from dust, and He describes the stages through which that dust passed, such as its becoming clay that clings (*ṭīnan lāziban*), black mud moulded into shape (*ḥama'an masnūnan*), and dry clay like pottery (*ṣalṣālan ka-al-fakhkhār*).

He also explains that He created that female, who is Hawwa', from that male, who is Adam. He said in Surat al-Nisa': ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from a single soul and created from it its mate and spread from the two of them many men and women﴾ [al-Nisa': 1]. He said, exalted is He, in al-A'raf: ﴿It is He who created you from a single soul and made from it its mate that he might find tranquillity in her﴾ [al-A'raf: 189]. And He said, exalted is He, in az-Zumar: ﴿He created you from a single soul; then He made from it its mate﴾ [az-Zumar: 6].

We have already mentioned that He created the human species in four different types:

The first: He created him neither from a female nor from a male, and this is Adam (peace be upon him).

The second: He created him from a male without a female, and this is Hawwa'.

The third: He created him from a female without a male, and this is 'Isa (upon him and upon our Prophet be prayers and peace).

The fourth: He created him from a male and a female, and this is all the rest of the children of Adam. This indicates the completeness of His power, exalted is He.

**Issue (*mas'alah*)**

These Qur'anic verses mentioned indicate that the first woman's initial existence was dependent upon and derived from the existence of the man.

This is a cosmic, divinely decreed matter from Allah, by which He brought the woman into existence in her first creation from him.

The noble Shari'ah revealed from Allah came to be acted upon on His earth, taking this cosmic, decreed matter into account in the life of the woman in all respects.

So He made the man a guardian over her, and made her dependent upon him in all her affairs, as He said, exalted is He: [p. 415] ﴿Men are the protectors of women﴾ [al-Nisa': 34], and the verse continues.

Therefore, the attempt to make women equal with men in all aspects of life cannot be realized, because the differences between the two sexes, first in creation and decree, and second in the revealed Shari'ah, prevent that absolutely.

Because of the strength of the cosmic, decreed and legislative differences between the male and the female, it is authentically reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he cursed the one of either sex who imitates the other.

There is no doubt that the reason for this curse is the attempt by those who wish to imitate the other, aiming to break these differences which cannot be broken.

It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the men who imitate women and the women who imitate men."

We have previously presented this hadith with its chain in Surat Bani Isra'il, and we explained there that whoever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) curses is cursed in the Book of Allah. So if the differences between the male and the female could be broken and removed, the one who wished that would not deserve the curse from Allah and His Messenger.

And because of those great cosmic and decreed differences between the male and the female, Allah, exalted is He, distinguished between them in divorce, making it in the hand of the man and not the woman; and in inheritance; and in attributing children to him.

And in the plurality of wives but not of husbands: He declared that the testimony of two women is equivalent to the testimony of one man, in His saying: ﴿If there are not two men, then a man and two women﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282]. So Allah, who created them both, is without doubt most knowing of their reality, and He declared in His Book that a man stands in the place of two women in testimony.

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Is for you the male and for Him the female? That, then, is an unjust division﴾ [an-Najm: 21–22], meaning unjust, because the two shares are not equal, due to the superiority of the male over the female.

For this reason the wife of 'Imran fell into a difficulty when she gave birth to Maryam, as Allah said about her: ﴿So when she delivered her, she said, "My Lord, I have delivered her a female," and Allah knew best what she delivered, "and the male is not like the female"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 36]. So the wife of 'Imran says: "and the male is not like the female," and she is without doubt truthful in that.

[p. 416] The disbelievers and their followers say that the male and the female are the same.

There is no doubt for every intelligent person in the truth of this negative proposition and the falsity of that affirmative one.

We have explained, in Surat Bani Isra'il, in discussing His saying: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright﴾ [al-Isra': 9], the wisdom behind making divorce in the hand of the man, preferring the male over the female in inheritance, plurality of wives, and the child being attributed to the man. We mentioned a portion of that in Surat al-Baqarah, in discussing His saying: ﴿And for the men over them is a degree﴾ [al-Baqarah: 228]. We clarified that the natural differences between them are that maleness is nobility, perfection, and natural, moral strength, while femaleness is the opposite of that.

We clarified that intelligent people all agree in acknowledging this, and that among the clearest proofs that the Qur'an presented for this is the consensus of intelligent people that from the time of her upbringing a female is adorned with kinds of ornament, such as jewellery and finery, to compensate for the innate natural deficiency that is femaleness, as the poet said:

Jewellery is nothing but an adornment for a deficiency, completing a beauty when beauty falls short.

We have explained that Allah, exalted is He, clarified this by His saying: ﴿Is one who is brought up among ornaments, and in dispute is not clear?﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 18]. He rebuked the disbelievers for claiming that He has offspring, while they assigned to Him the lesser and weaker of the two offspring in creation and nature, which is the female.

For this reason, she is raised among ornaments from her childhood, to cover the deficiency that is femaleness and to compensate for it with adornment, so she is "not clear in dispute."

Because the female, due to her natural, innate weakness, cannot make her case clear in dispute as the strong males do, when she is oppressed and wronged because of her natural weakness.

Allah's rebuke of the disbelievers, that while claiming offspring for Him they assigned to Him the lesser and weaker of the two, is frequent in the Qur'an,

- such as His saying: ﴿Has He chosen daughters over sons? What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ [as-Saffat: 153–154],
- and His saying: ﴿Has your Lord then preferred you with sons and taken from the angels females? Indeed, you say a tremendous saying﴾ [al-Isra': 40],
- and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Had Allah intended to take a son, He would have chosen from what He creates whatever He wills﴾ [az-Zumar: 4].

The verses of this kind are many and well known.

[p. 417] As for the male, he is not raised among ornaments, because the perfection of his maleness, its nobility, and his natural strength do not need, with him, the adornment with jewellery that the female needs, since he is perfect in his maleness and she is deficient in her femaleness.

And among matters on which intelligent people have no dispute: when the male and the female live together in the normal human, natural association without which mankind cannot survive, the woman is affected by that with a natural, cosmic, decreed effect that prevents her from undertaking work, such as pregnancy, childbirth, and what arises from that of weakness, sickness, and pain.

Unlike the man, who is not affected by any of that. With these differences, no one dares to say that they are equal in all fields except a person who is obstinate against what is evident to the senses. No one calls for equality between them except one whose insight Allah has blinded.

We have, in the two passages of this blessed book to which we have pointed, presented what suffices the fair-minded, so there is no need to repeat it here.

* * *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another﴾.

Since His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have created you from male and female﴾ [al-Hujurat: 13] indicates the equality of people in origin, because their father is one and their mother is one, and in that is the greatest restraint against boasting of lineages and some people's arrogance over others, He, exalted is He, made clear that He made them into peoples and tribes so that they would come to know one another, that is, some of them know others and are distinguished from others, not so that some of them boast over others and act arrogantly toward them.

This indicates that some being better and more noble than others comes from another cause than lineages.

Allah made this clear here by His saying: ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah﴾ [al-Hujurat: 13]. From this it becomes clear that superiority and nobility come only from piety toward Allah, not from anything else such as affiliation to tribes. He who said the truth said:

Islam has raised Salman the Persian, and disbelief has lowered the noble Abu Lahab.

They mention that Salman, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say:

My father is Islam; I have no other father, when they boast of Qays or Tamim.

These Qur'anic verses indicate that the religion of Islam is divine and true, and no consideration is given in it to colours, to races, or to regions. What is considered in it is the piety and obedience of Allah, exalted and majestic is He. The most noble and most excellent of people is the most pious of them toward Allah, and there is no nobility or superiority for one who is not pious, even if he is of high lineage.

The word *shu'ub* is the plural of *sha'b*, which is the first level of the six levels that the Arabs use, and they are: *sha'b* (people/nation), *qabīlah* (tribe), *'imārah* (clan), *baṭn* (sub-clan), *fakhdh* (thigh/division), and *faṣīlah* (close family).

So the *sha'b* gathers the tribes, the tribe gathers the clans, the clan gathers the sub-clans, the sub-clan gathers the thighs, and the thigh gathers the close families.

Khuzaymah is a *sha'b*, Kinanah is a tribe, Quraysh is a clan, Qusayy is a sub-clan, Hashim is a thigh, and al-'Abbas is a close family.

The *shu'ub* were so named because the tribes branch out (*tatashha''ab*) from them. End of quotation.

Of these six, only three are mentioned in the Qur'an: the *shu'ub* and the *qaba'il*, as in this verse, and the *faṣīlah* in al-Ma'arij, in His saying: ﴿and his close family that shelters him﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 13]. We have already presented what these verses indicate, clarified in Surat Bani Isra'il in discussing His saying: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright﴾ [al-Isra': 9].

Know that the Arabs sometimes use some of these six to refer to others, such as using *baṭn* to refer to a tribe, in the words of the poet:

Indeed, Kilab, these are ten sub-clans, and you are innocent of their ten tribes.

As we have presented in Surat al-Baqarah, in discussing His saying: ﴿three periods﴾ [al-Baqarah: 228].

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab*:

[p. 398] In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Surat al-Hujurat.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female﴾.

This noble verse indicates that the beginning of the creation of mankind is from a male and a female.

Other verses have indicated their creation from other than that, such as His saying: ﴿It is He who created you from dust﴾ [Ghafir: 67], and His saying: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust﴾ [al-Hajj: 5].

The answer is clear, which is that dust is the first stage, and He has said: ﴿And He has created you in stages﴾ [Nuh: 14].

Allah has explained the stages of the creation of man from his beginning to his end by His saying: ﴿And We did certainly create man from an extract of clay. Then We made him a sperm-drop in a firm place﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 12–13], to the end of it.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed; rather say, 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts."﴾

In this noble verse, He, exalted and majestic, mentions that these Bedouins, who are the people of the desert among the Arabs (p-419), said, "We have believed." Allah, exalted and majestic, commanded His Prophet to say to them: ﴿You have not believed; rather say, "We have submitted"﴾. This indicates the negation of faith from them and the affirmation of Islam for them.

This implies that faith (*iman*) is more specific than Islam, because the negation of the more specific does not necessitate the negation of the more general.

We have previously stated many times that the legal (*shar'i*) true meaning of faith and the legal true meaning of Islam is the submission of the heart through belief, the tongue through affirmation, and the limbs through action. Their referent is one, as His saying, exalted is He, indicates: ﴿So We brought out those who were in it of the believers. But We found not there except one house of the submitters [Muslims]﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 35–36].

Since this is so, it is necessary to explain the distinction between faith and Islam in this noble verse, because Allah negated faith from them but not Islam. There are two well-known explanations among the scholars for this. The one that appears most correct to me is that the faith negated from them in this verse is its legal true meaning, and the Islam affirmed for them in it is the linguistic Islam (*al-Islam al-lughawi*), which is submission and compliance by the limbs without the heart.

The linguistic literal meaning (*al-haqiqa al-lughawiyya*) of Islam was permitted here, even though the legal literal meaning (*al-haqiqa al-shar'iyya*) takes precedence over the linguistic one according to the correct view, because the noble Law was based on what is apparent, and all inner secrets are left to Allah.

So the compliance of the limbs outwardly through action and of the tongue through affirmation is sufficient in the Law, even if the heart harbors disbelief.

For this reason, it was permitted to intend the linguistic literal meaning in His saying: ﴿but say, "We have submitted"﴾, because the compliance of the tongue and limbs outwardly is linguistic Islam, which is sufficient in the Law without searching into the heart.

Every compliance, submission and humble acceptance is called Islam linguistically. From this is the saying of Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl al-'Adawi, a Muslim of the pre-Islamic era (*Jahiliyya*):

I have submitted my face to Him to whom the earth has submitted, bearing heavy boulders,
He spread it out, and when it became level, He fixed it firmly, together, and set the mountains upon it.
I have submitted my face to Him to whom the clouds have submitted, bearing sweet, pure water,
When they are driven to a land, they obey and pour down their rain upon it in abundance.
I have submitted my face to Him to whom the wind has submitted, turning from state to state.

(p-420) So what is meant by Islam in these verses is submission and compliance. If Islam in His saying, "but say, 'We have submitted'" is understood as "we have complied and submitted with the tongues and limbs," then there is no difficulty in the verse.

According to this view, the Bedouins mentioned are hypocrites (*munafiqun*), because they are Muslims outwardly while they are disbelievers inwardly.

The second explanation: the negation of faith in His saying "You have not believed" means the negation of the perfection of faith, not its negation from its very root.

Accordingly, there is also no difficulty, because they are Muslims while their faith is not complete. This presents no difficulty for the People of the Sunna and the Community (*Ahl al-Sunna wa al-Jama'a*), who hold that faith increases and decreases.

We have only favored the first explanation, namely that Islam is meant in its linguistic sense and not its legal sense, and that the Bedouins mentioned are disbelievers inwardly even though they have submitted outwardly. This is because His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾ [al-Hujurat: 14] indicates this with a clear indication, as you see. This is because His saying "yadkhul" (*yadkhulu*, "enter") is a verb in the context of negation, and it is among the forms of generality, as we have explained many times. The author of *Maraqi al-Su'ud* alludes to this with his words:

And like "I did not drink" or "if he drinks," and they agreed that the verbal noun (*masdar*) draws in [generality] if it is [in the context of negation].

So His saying, "and faith has not yet entered your hearts," means: there is no entry of faith into your hearts.

Those who held the second view said: the meaning of the negation of its entry is the negation of its perfection, but the first view is more apparent, as you see.

His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿The Bedouins say﴾: what is meant by it is some of the Bedouins. We have favored that they are hypocrites, because the Qur'an indicates this. They are of the same kind as the Bedouins about whom Allah said: ﴿And among the Bedouins are those who consider what they spend as a loss and await misfortunes to befall you﴾ [at-Tawba: 98]. We only said that what is meant in this verse is some of the Bedouins, because Allah explained in another place that among them are some who are not like that, and that is in His saying, exalted is He: (p-421) ﴿And among the Bedouins are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day and consider what they spend as means of nearness to Allah and blessings of the Messenger. Unquestionably, it is a means of nearness for them. Allah will admit them into His mercy. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [at-Tawba: 99].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 49, verse 16:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Will you inform Allah of your religion? And Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and Allah is Knowing of all things."﴾ When these Bedouins said, "We have believed," and Allah commanded His Prophet to refute them in His saying, ﴿Say: "You have not believed"﴾ and His saying, ﴿while faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾, He commanded their Prophet to say to them, in the form of a rebuke: ﴿Will you inform Allah of your religion?﴾ This is because of your claim that you are believers, while Allah is not hidden from anything of your state. He knows that you have not believed, He knows everything in the heavens and the earth, and He knows all things.

What this noble verse includes of condemning the self-purification through falsehood has come clarified in other places, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He knows you best since He produced you from the earth and when you were fetuses in the bellies of your mothers. So do not claim purity for yourselves; He knows best who fears Allah.﴾ [An-Najm: 32], and the verses of similar meaning are many and well known.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 49, verse 18:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in the beginning of Surat Hud, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Unquestionably, they fold their chests to hide from Him. Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾ [Hud: 5].
